newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-AUXERRE GO THROUGH AT FIRST ATTEMPT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUXERRE GO THROUGH AT FIRST ATTEMPT.

text.p: Auxerre reached the European Cup quarter-finals at the first attempt when they beat Glasgow Rangers 2-1 at home in their final Champions' League group A match on Wednesday.
The French champions surprisingly ended up winning a very tight group and will meet group B runners-up Borussia Dortmund of Germany in the last eight next March.
First-half goals by central striker Lilian Laslandes and wing Steve Marlet, his second of the competition, secured victory for Auxerre.

Rangers captain Richard Gough, in his last European tie for the Scottish club he is quitting at the end of the season, brought his side back into the game with a header from a free kick nine minutes before the interval.
The width of goalkeeper Fabien Cool's post stood between Auxerre winning the group or finishing second when it denied Rangers left back David Robertson a 75th minute equaliser.

Rangers' only telling mark on the Champions' League was a surprise home win over Grasshopper Zurich in their previous match that contributed to the Swiss side's elimination after they had emerged as group favourites.
